subject.title: fix(web-shared): treat exact-limit response reads as complete

question: Should `readResponseText` ever read past `maxBytes` to prove exact-limit completeness, and if so under what bounded contract?
rationale: A prior same-shape PR was closed by a repository member pending explicit content-length/overread contract or real failing-response proof, and this PR repeats an unguarded post-cap read that can affect availability.

options.title: Require a bounded contract
options.body: Accept the fix direction only with content-length or idle-bounded overflow proof plus tests for exact, empty post-cap, stalled, and overflow streams.

options.title: Keep the fail-closed cap
options.body: Leave current cap behavior in place until a real failing response proves that exact-limit completeness must be distinguished.

options.title: Accept the one-read overread
options.body: Own the timeout/availability tradeoff from waiting for one more stream result after `maxBytes`.

recommendation.title: Require a bounded contract
recommendation.body: Accept the fix direction only with content-length or idle-bounded overflow proof plus tests for exact, empty post-cap, stalled, and overflow streams.

likelyOwner.reason: He is assigned here and already made the same-cluster contract/proof decision on the earlier PR.
